summary:
# NOTES: THE QUEEN OF THE ISLE; OR, A HASTY WOOING (May Agnes Fleming, 1886)

Single novel, no separate books. Chapters I–XXXV, plus an end note.

## Front matter
Title page: "The Queen of the Isle: A Novel" by May Agnes Fleming. Publisher G. W. Dillingham (successor to G. W. Carleton & Co.), New York; London: S. Low, Son & Co., 1886.

## Characters (key)
- **Guy Campbell** – "Captain Guy," last Campbell, owner of Campbell's Isle, schooner *Evening Star*, tall, dark, bold; sister Sibyl. Aged ~23.
- **Sibyl Campbell** – "Queen of the Isle," ~17, beautiful, dark Syrian/gipsy looks, black hair, fiery, proud, jealous.
- **Willard Drummond** – half-American, half-Parisian, heir to Virginia estate, Sibyl's lover, faithless; father dies later.
- **Christie** (Christina Tomlinson) – ~16, golden hair, blue eyes, niece (really foundling) of Mrs. Tom; secretly married to Willard; later revealed as Sibyl's half-sister, daughter of Bertha and Mark Campbell.
- **Mrs. Tom (Mrs. Tomlinson)** – tiny (4 ft), brisk, thrifty, talkative widow; hates laziness; kicks cat Trot; nephew Carl.
- **Carl Henley** – ~15, lazy, yellow-haired, dull blue eyes; plays Jew's harp; later marries German girl.
- **Aunt Moll** and son **Lem** – black servants at Campbell's Lodge; Lem described as lazy, half-simple.
- **Richard Grove** – dying passenger, ex-mason, witness to walling-up; dies in Mrs. Tom's cottage.
- **Rev. Mark Brantwell** and **Mrs. Harriet Brantwell** – Episcopal clergyman and jolly wife in N----; Sibyl's hosts.
- **Laura Britton / Laura Courtney** – "Madcap Laura," pretty, pert; Willard's old flame; married to **Edgar Courtney**.
- **Edgar Courtney** – jealous, sour, tyrannical husband; wounded in wreck; kills (he thinks) Laura, actually stabs Christie.
- **Will Stafford** – Sibyl's admirer; sees Willard's secret wedding; later rides to deliver news.
- **Mark Campbell** – late master of the lodge, violent, murderous father of Christie; married secretly to Bertha.
- **Sir Guy the Fearless** – legendary freebooter, founder line.
- **Bertha** – Spanish-born (Grenada) maniac, cousin of **Reuben Deerwood**; Christie's mother.
- **Reuben Deerwood** – Quaker-speaking, large, kind, ~40s, cousin of Bertha, keeps her in forest hut.
- **Sheriff Lawless**; lawyer **C. Ringdon**; judge; counsel **Mr. P----**; warden **Mr. Dent**; **Mr. Lawless**.
- Egyptian astrologer (Germany) prophesied Willard's four visions: wedding (bride = Sibyl), prison-cell with chained woman in bridal robes, murder in wood by lightning, scaffold hanging of a woman.
- Other: Johnny and Sary (farm family); Jonathan (farm man); Jenny (mulatto maid), Tom (boy); Trot the cat.

## Setting
Campbell's Isle, ~6 miles off M---- coast (Atlantic), ~2 miles across. Campbell's Lodge (dark, dilapidated, rumored haunted). Mrs. Tom's cottage on a rise. Westport (town, dock-yard, Westbrook House/Westport House hotel, Methodist chapel). N---- (Brantwell parsonage). New York. Forest hut of Reuben.

## Plot in order
1. **Ch I**: Island history; Sir Guy took Spanish girl; Gasper; Mark Campbell (dark, feared); Guy inherits ~3 years before; Aunt Moll and Lem left in lodge; Mrs. Tom and Carl, Christie (mystery origin), dog, parrot.
2. **Ch II**: On *Evening Star*, Guy and Willard talk; Richard Grove, sick passenger, picked up in Liverpool. Sibyl appears. Willard's Egyptian vision story (four visions). Moon-cloud omen. Willard reveals Sibyl is the bride/prisoner-woman; "_You_, Sibyl."
3. **Ch III**: Landing; Mrs. Tom nurses Grove. Grove's deathbed confession: ~13 years ago, overheard plot, blindfolded, taken to a house; saw murdered youth; walled up woman (who cursed) and murdered body in closet; paid to swear silence. Grove dies, sees face at window.
4. **Ch IV**: Lodge described; Aunt Moll and Lem absent; Willard given "haunted" room; ghost tales; midnight visit—white ghost with cold hand; Willard finds door locked.
5. **Ch V**: Mrs. Tom wakes Carl to sit with corpse; Guy disbelieves story; Sibyl and Willard decide to change rooms. Sibyl also heard midnight cry/fall.
6. **Ch VI**: Brantwells (Mark and Harriet) arrive; Mr. Brantwell looks like Willard's vision bridegroom. Sibyl taken to N----. Willard meets Christie singing on rocks; visits cottage; pressed to be enchanted.
7. **Ch VII**: Guy leaves for Westbrook (Evening Star repairs). Willard woos Christie in woods; Christie is "fairest"; Carl interrupts.
8. **Ch VIII**: Aunt Moll gossip with Lem. Willard proposes marriage to Christie under willow; she accepts ("Willard"). Plan to marry secretly at Westport.
9. **Ch IX**: Mrs. Tom sends Christie for tea; Willard rows her to Westport; Methodist chapel marriage. Christie seized by sudden vision of Sibyl's eyes and knife. Phantom in pine woods cries "murdered! murdered!"; Christie faints.
10. **Ch X**: Guy at Westport hotel reads advertisement (C. Ringdon, estate of uncle Richard Eyre, New York banker). Stafford saw secret marriage. Guy and Stafford go to Brantwells; Sibyl told of inheritance; both sail to New York.
11. **Ch XI**: Willard neglects Sibyl; Lem and Carl; great storm; wreck of ship; minute-gun; Willard and Carl rescue Laura Courtney and Edgar Courtney; bodies laid before fire.
12. **Ch XII**: Laura (Britton) Courtney recognized in cottage; Edgar jealous, suspicious. Willard leaves with Lem to Westport for doctor. Sibyl returns home; Aunt Moll tells Sibyl of Willard and Christie. Sibyl goes to cottage at night.
13. **Ch XIII**: Sibyl confronts Christie; demands she give up Willard; Christie refuses ("I love him!"); Sibyl threatens; Christie faints. Sibyl collapses at lodge.
14. **Ch XIV**: Edgar's jealous exchanges with Laura; Christie confronts Willard, is "wife"-claiming? (Willard placates). Captain Campbell flirts with Laura; Laura announces she'll go to island Thursday; Edgar angry.
15. **Ch XV**: Sibyl returns to N----; Brantwell party; Edgar watches jealously; Laura sings "Oh, had we some bright little isle of our own."
16. **Ch XVI**: Sibyl confronts Willard in conservatory; he lies; she believes him; "I swear."
17. **Ch XVII**: Laura to stay at Brantwells; Edgar threatens. Guy told Laura to visit island Thursday. Willard stays in Westport. Edgar hears Laura's appointment.
18. **Ch XVIII**: Willard writes note to Christie (lost; Edgar finds it under Laura's chair). Christie sends counter-note to Sibyl via Guy ("I did not tell you all that night..."). Sibyl wants to go to island. Edgar beats/throws Laura into table; she bleeds. Edgar leaves in boat with Lem-like boy (half-simple).
19. **Ch XIX**: Mrs. Brantwell scolds Sibyl. Laura found bleeding. Willard receives news of father's illness and leaves Virginia. Sibyl sails with Carl at storm approach.
20. **Ch XX**: Storm. Sibyl reaches lodge; Aunt Moll and Lem terrified. Shriek of "Murder!" at midnight.
21. **Ch XXI**: Edgar waits at trysting spot. Christie goes out in storm to meet Willard. Edgar believes it's Laura, believes she has come to meet a lover, stabs Christie. Sees a female ghost-like figure flee crying "Murder!"; Edgar flees.
22. **Ch XXII**: Edgar takes boy back to Westport; hires gig; arrives N----; finds Laura alive. Collapses.
23. **Ch XXIII**: Sibyl searches island; finds bloody handkerchief marked "Christina." Mrs. Tom discovers Christie missing; Carl saw woman flying "murder." Sibyl and Mrs. Tom go to N----.
24. **Ch XXIV**: Christie wakes in Reuben's forest cabin; Reuben (Quaker, "thee") nursed her; Bertha (maniac) in cabin.
25. **Ch XXV**: Reuben tells Bertha's history (Grenada, school, Mark Campbell's secret marriage, Mark's jealousy, Bertha's child, Reuben rescues Bertha from lodge trap room; Mark died later).
26. **Ch XXVI**: Edgar awakes; Laura alive; Edgar questions; hears Christie murdered; Laura suspects Carl's woman sighting; Edgar plans to frame Sibyl; cannot sleep.
27. **Ch XXVII**: Willard returns after father's death (Virginia), resolves to confess; meets Guy at Westbrook. Learns of Christie's death; grief. Sibyl and Willard reconciled, plan Europe trip.
28. **Ch XXVIII**: Europe tour; return; wedding at N---- church. Sheriff Lawless interrupts: charge Sibyl with Christie's murder on warrant from Edgar Courtney. Mrs. Tom shrieks.
29. **Ch XXIX**: Sibyl arrested, taken to county jail; Willard follows. Brantwells and Stafford distressed; Stafford rides to Westport.
30. **Ch XXX**: Mrs. Brantwell sick. Stafford reports trial: witnesses Methodist minister (married Willard to Christina), Mrs. Tom, Guy, Carl (saw woman), Edgar (testimony). Sibyl guilty; death sentence by hanging. Sibyl says "Not guilty" at start.
31. **Ch XXXI**: Guy and Mrs. Brantwell visit Sibyl; she is mad in prison cell.
32. **Ch XXXII**: Willard rides away; falls ill at farm; overhears Sibyl's execution set for day after; rides; falls from horse in storm; Bertha finds him; Christie appears.
33. **Ch XXXIII**: Christie, consumptive, finds Willard wounded; Reuben and Bertha bring him to cabin. Christie identifies herself as wife.
34. **Ch XXXIV**: Willard and Christie talk; Christie forgives; Willard denies being at the island; they leave for Westport in donkey-cart, then farm wagon; horse dies; they race; reprieve waved; arrive at scaffold; Christie rises.
35. **Ch XXXV**: Edgar collapses, bleeding, dies (confessed stabbing, mistook Christie for Laura). Sibyl reprieved; she refuses Willard, then, at Christie's dying request, reconciles. Christie dies at window. Mrs. Tom reveals Christie is Bertha's child by Mark Campbell and Sibyl's half-sister. Epilogue: Sibyl and Willard marry a year later; Laura marries Guy and sails to Europe; Reuben and Bertha; Carl marries German girl; Mrs. Tom remains on island.

## Key quoted phrases
"Queen of the Isle"; "Off with the Old Love, and on with the New"; "Murder!"; "Not guilty! your honor"; "Guilty!"; "_You_, Sibyl--_you!_"; "I curse you!" (Bertha); "Christie, Christie!" (Willard); "A reprieve! a reprieve!"
